title: Attention heads selected on symbols also affected evidence judgments in text
summary: Ablating eight Pythia-410M attention heads chosen using symbolic prompts reduced accuracy on a natural-language evidence task by 8.2 percentage points. Ablating random sets matched by layer and size reduced it by 0.8 points. A separate full-precision analysis showed an effect in the same direction.
ai_technology: Pythia-410M; attention-head ablation; related native full-precision models

evidence.tested: The study selected the eight heads without natural-language prompts, then compared ablation on held-out domains and paraphrases. The original comparison averaged five seeds.
evidence.unknown: The task asks which state has more supporting reports. The result establishes influence under intervention in these models, not a general account of reasoning or identical head functions across models.
evidence.ai_role: The learned attention heads were selected using controlled changes in symbolic evidence and then intervened on during a separate natural-language evidence comparison.
